state:
Goal `tools-cli`: seven features of `docs/reference/tools/10-cli.md` now have all their proofs. This
session finished `nvs-config-check-and-nvs-config-dump`. Its attack found a bug, and the bug is
fixed. A value or a table name holding a newline printed across several rows of `nvs config dump`,
so it could forge a row such as `limits.hard.memory = "99G"`. `nvs_config::audit` now spells every
key and value on one line with TOML escapes, and `nvs ctl config` shares that renderer.
`bun nv proofs --owed | grep tools:cli` lists the six features still owed. Two of them also owe
`help`: `nvs-build-compile` and `nvs-build-openapi`.

items.text: **`tools:cli/nvs-build-compile`** — owes examples, help, hostile, tests (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`). `docs/reference/tools/10-cli.md:259`. For help, add a fenced block showing the command and what it writes. Look for existing `--compile` tests in `crates/nvs-cli/tests/bundle.rs` that need only a `// covers:` marker.

**`tools:cli/nvs-build-openapi`** — owes examples, help, hostile, tests (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`). `docs/reference/tools/10-cli.md:280`. `crates/nvs-cli/tests/openapi.rs` may already hold tests that need only a `// covers:` marker. The attack for `nvs-api-diff` already builds routes that are hard to write into an API document. Reuse it only if this feature's test needs different assertions.

backlog: `tools:cli/one-binary`, `nvs-run`, `nvs-check` and `nvs-test` each owe examples, hostile and tests (`docs/reference/tools/10-cli.md`).

`Core\Config::set` returns `true` for a name no setting reads, such as `limits.memoryX` or one holding a newline: the `limits` block row governs every `limits.<anything>` (`crates/nvs-config/src/directive.rs:283`). The value only reaches the request's own overlay. Whether a block row may govern an unknown leaf belongs to `rule:config/ini-set-is-core-config-set` (`crates/nvs-config/src/request.rs:101`).
`nvs config dump` sorts numbered blocks as text, so `app.10` prints before `app.2`. The chapter says "dotted-key order", which this is. `crates/nvs-config/src/audit.rs` owns the order.
The `E0601` note for a table header prints the header cut at its first dot: `in [log.` for `[log.handler."x"]`. *not checked* where the note is built.
`nvs info | head -1` in PowerShell exited 255, which may be a panic on a closed pipe (`crates/nvs-cli/src/info.rs:53`). *not checked* under a POSIX shell.
